full_judgment:
2. The petitioner filed the writ petition stating that he is an Advocate by profession and former President of the Supreme Court Bar Association. He was one of the founders of the political party, Bangladesh Nationalist Party (B.N.P). He was the member of the first Standing Committee of B.N.P., President of Dhaka District B.N.P. and Vice President of B.N.P. Central Committee. He was Food Minister, Information Minister and Communication Minister. He is also the founder of Bangladesh Society for the Enforcement of Human Rights (BSEHR) and is actively engaged in many social and cultural association of the country. While he was the Member of Parliament he applied to the District Magistrate, Dhaka for issuance of license of 2 fire arms for his own safety. Considering the status of the petitioner, respondent No.2 issued the licence of a revolver bearing No.44-I 9-95 dated 24.09.1995 in reference to the order of the Ministry of Home Affairs vide Memo No.19(Act)-95 (Raj 4)-868 dated 24.9.1995 corresponding to File No. Arm (76-Revolver) 95 and the said licence was being renewed from time to time by his Security Officer, Major Wadud (Retired). After declaration of State of Emergency on 11.1.2007 by the then care taker Government a joint task force raided the residence of the petitioner and took many valuable articles and cash money without preparing any seizure list and arrested him. Criminal Case being Dhanmondi Police Station Case No.29 dated 8.3.2007 under section 19A of the Arms Act, 1878 was started against him. Pursuant to the direction of the Government vide Memo No. বিবিধ ৯(২)/২০০৬ (রাজ-৬)১২৯১ dated 24.12.2006 the petitioner deposited 2 fire arms and ammunitions including the instant revolver with the Dohar Police Station being G.D. Entry No.1222 dated 28.12.2006 along with the licences. The petitioner had all the reason to believe that his licence was already renewed. From the contents of the First Information Report of the said criminal case the petitioner came to know that the licence of the revolver had been cancelled as the same was not renewed after expiry on 4.6.2003 by the District Magistrate, Dhaka respondent No.2 vide Memo No. ঢাকা/আর্মস/৬৫ বিবিধ-২০০২/১৮৫(১০) dated 07.3.2007. Before cancellation of the licence no notice as required under section 18 of the Arms Act was served upon the petitioner nor he was given any opportunity of being heard. Thus the impugned order of cancellation of licence, though not served upon the  petitioner, was passed in violation of section 18 of the Altos Act, 1878 and the principles of natural justice and as such the same is liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 4. Mr. Nazmul Huda, the learned Advocate, the petitioner appearing in person submits that the licence of his revolver bearing No.44-I9-95 dated 24.9.1995 was cancelled by the District Magistrate, Dhaka, the respondent No.2 by the impugned order contained in Memo No. ঢাকা/আর্মস/৬৫ বিবিধ-২০০২/১৮৫(১০) dated 073.2007 on the allegation of non-renewal of  licence since 4.10.2003 as contained in Annexure-A to the writ petition in violation of section 18 of the Arms Act, 1878 and Rule 42 of the Arms Rules, 1924 as no notice asking him to show cause as to why his said licence would not be cancelled nor given him any opportunity of being heard. He in support of his contention referred to the cases decided by this Court in the case of Sheikh Ali Ahmed Vs. Secretary of Ministry of Home Affairs reported in 40 DLR(AD) 170 and the case of Rezaul Karim Vs. Secretary of Ministry of Home Affairs and others reported in 44 DLR 110. He also submits that the proceeding of Criminal Case being Metropolitan Sessions Tribunal Case No.301 of 2007 arising out of Dhanmondi Police Station Case, No.29 dated 83.2007 under section 19A of the Arms Act, 1878 (Annexure-A to the writ petition) was quashed by another Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.7181 of 2007 by the judgment and order dated 16.7.2009. Thus he submits that the impugned order dated 8.3.2007 (as contained in Annexure-A to the writ petition) passed by the respondent No.2 is liable to be declarer to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect by making the Rule absolute. 

 5. Mr. Md. Nazrul Talukder, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the respondents submits that as the petitioner's revolver licence expired long before on 4.10.2003 and for non-renewal his licence was cancelled by the District Magistrate, Dhaka, the respondent No.2 by the impugned order dated 7.3.2010 as contained in Annexure-A to the writ petition, the First Information Report in Dhanmondi Police Station Case No.29 dated 8.3.2007. Since the licence was not in existence from 4.10.2003 the petitioner was not entitled to any notice or being heard in person before cancellation of the licence. The respondent No.2 did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned order dated 7.3.2007 cancelling the petitioner's revolver licence and hence the Rule should be discharged. 

 8. Before we proceed to consider the merit of the case it will be proper to reproduce the relevant provisions relating to cancellation of arms licence for better understanding. Section 18 of the Arms Act, 1878 provides us under:- 

 Provided that where a license is granted in Form XV, XVI, XVIII or XIX for the possession of arms to be acquired by the licensee subsequently to the grant of the license, the authority granting the license shall at the time of granting the same direct that within a period specified by him in this behalf, which he may from time to time extend, the arms covered by the license shall be acquired and that the license or the arms or both shall be produced for his inspection, and if within the period of specified or extended the license fails to acquire the arms and to produce the license or the arms or both as the case may be the license shall cause to be in force. 

 (c) The authority issuing a license will ordinarily be responsible for watching all future renewals of the license. Where a license is renewed by an authority other than the authority who granted it, the former shall forthwith inform the latter of the fact of renewal and the period for which such renewal is valid. The applicant for the renewal of license under this proviso should however, always be required to state his permanent residence, and if he notifies a change in this permanent residence to the district in which the renewal is sought, the licensing authority of such district shall thenceforward become responsible for watching all future renewals of his license and shall inform the original issuing authority accordingly. This procedure shall be repeated on each subsequent occasion of renewal of the license, the necessary intimation being sent by the renewing authority to the original issuing authority or to the authority who last renewed the license on a permanent change of address, as the case may be." 

 11. In the case of Sk. Ali Ahmed Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs reported in 40 DLR(AD) 170 their Lordships of the Appellate Division held as under:- 

 12. In the instant case no reasons for cancellation of the petitioner's revolver license was communicated. The respondents even did not lay before this Court the reasons for cancellation by filling affidavit-in-opposition or by producing the relevant file of the Government to consider what prompted the respondent No.2 in taking decision of cancellation of the license of the petitioner. 

 13. The impugned order of cancellation was not even communicated to the petitioner. From the First Information Report of Dhanmondi Police Station Case No.29 dated 8.3.2007 (Annexure-A to the writ petition) it appears that the license No.44/19/1995 dated 24.4.1995 for the revolver granted to the petitioner was cancelled by the District Magistrate, Dhaka, the respondent No.2 by memo. No. Dhaka/Arms/65/Misc/2002- 185(10) dated 7.3.2010 for the allegation of non-renewal of the said license, expired 4.10.2003 for the year 2004, 2005, 2006 and 2007. The petitioner challenging the proceedings of the said criminal case for quashing moved this Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.7181 of 2009 and the Rule issued earlier was made absolute quashing the proceeding of the said criminal case by judgment and order dated 16.7.2009 passed by a Division Bench of this Court (Annexure-D to the supplementary affidavit dated 083.2010). While disposing the said case their Lordships found as under:- 

 14. "No one should be condemned unheard," is a settled principle of law which is embodied in the maxim audi altemm parkin. What these principles of natural justice are it is not possible to lay down with any exactness. In the case of The University of Dhaka Vs. Zakir Ahmed (popularly known as Zakir Ahmed's Case) reported in 16 DLR (SC) 722 Supreme Court of Pakistan held as under:- 

 "Nevertheless, the general consensus of judicial opinion seems to be that in order to ensure the "elementary and essential principles of fairness" as a matter of necessary implication, the person sought to be affected must at least be made aware of the nature of the allegation against him, he should be given a fair opportunity to make any relevant statement putting forward his own case to correct or controvert any relevant statement brought forward to his prejudice." 

 15. In the case of Sk. Ali Ahmed Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs reported in 40 DLR (AD) 170 our Appellate Division held as under: 

 "In all proceedings by whosoever held, whether judicial or administrative, the principles of natural justice have to be observed if the proceeding might result in consequences affecting "the person or property or other right of the parties concerned." This rule applies even although there may be no positive words in the statute or legal document whereby the power is vested to take such proceedings, for, in such cases this requirement is to be implied into it as the minimum requirement of fairness." 

 16. Relying on the aforesaid decision this Division in the case of Rezaul Karim (Md) and another Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and others reported in 40 DLR I 10 held as under:- 

 17. In the case in hand before cancellation of the license of the petitioner by the impugned order contained in Memo No. ঢাকা/আর্মস/৬৫ বিবিধ-২০০২/১৮৫(১০)dated  07.03.2003 as referred to in the First Information report of Dhanmondi Police Station Case No.29 dated 83.2007 (Annexure-A to the writ petition) passed by the District Magistrate, Dhaka, respondent No.2 in violation of section 18 of the Arms Act, 1878 read with rule 42 of the Arms Rules, 1924 and also in violation of the principles of natural justice and thus the same is liable to be declared to have been made and issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 20. The impugned order contained in Memo No. ঢাকা/আর্মস/৬৫ বিবিধ-২০০২/১৮৫(১০) dated 07.03.2003 as referred to in the First Information report of Dhanmondi Police Station Case No.29 dated 83.2007 (Annexure-A to the writ petition) is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
